rationale: Real B2B need and asset-light, but new entrant faces Xometry/Protolabs price anchoring; 15-30% markup, supplier willingness, and quality liability are all unverified. Net-30-60 receivables vs supplier prepay squeeze cash. Realistic yr3 profit ~$80-150k with two hires; disintermediation caps durability.
red_flags: New-entrant markup and supplier willingness are E assumptions
Incumbent Xometry is loss-making at 34.7% GM

rationale: Gain-share lowers buyer risk and capital is tiny, but fee %, achievable savings for sub-$3M shippers and retention are all unverified. Crowded field with incumbents holding far deeper benchmark data; revenue lapses after agreement term so book must be rebuilt. Boutique ceiling ~$1-3M revenue.
red_flags: Client churn after first renegotiation likely

rationale: Thin 8-15% net margins on inventory, Buy Box sharing, Amazon 1P and brand-revocation risk. Single-platform dependence and capital-hungry growth. Brand authorization for a newcomer is the real gate and is unverified. Realistic yr3 owner profit ~$30-70k on $50k inventory.

Mandate is A-level and recurring, but standalone consortium is a commoditized online price game with $50-120 per member contribution; would need thousands of members. Record itself says bundle-only. Pricing and lab/MRO wholesale rates MISSING.

Classic crowded broker vertical with tight reefer capacity and whole-load claim exposure; RFP-driven food shippers rarely award newcomers. $75k BMC-84 bond likely needs personal credit (unknown). Carriers paid before shippers pay. Realistic yr3 ~$60-150k if a desk is built; freight cyclicality.
red_flags: Bond affordability depends on founder credit

rationale: Strong B-level Item 19 revenue benchmark ($554k avg unit, $399/job) and paid-at-completion. Independent avoids royalties but must self-fund Google/LSA lead costs against three national brands. 2-3 truck metro operation plausibly yields ~$100-180k by yr3. Labor-heavy, local, municipal hauler licensing unchecked.
red_flags: Independent margins are E extrapolations of franchise data

rationale: Real ELDT mandate and employer demand, but tuition, WIOA caps, training-fleet insurance and IL SOS school licensing are all unverified. Capital in trucks, accident/insurance shocks, freight-cycle exposure and crowded field (community colleges, carrier-paid schools). Moderate single-yard economics.
red_flags: Tuition and per-student contribution are E

rationale: Extreme competition from Insureon, NEXT, Hiscox direct and others with better carrier access and ad budgets. CAC vs $75-450 commission and churn unverified; record itself shows $0 low case and 24-month breakeven. Producer license obtainable quickly but multi-state non-resident licensing adds cost.

Kforce A-level data confirms mechanics but shows 3.8% incumbent operating margin; boutique 22% GM is plausible. Founder tech vetting is a real wedge, yet field is extreme, VMS gates enterprises, and AI coding tools erode contract-dev demand. Float $15-20k per consultant strains cash; realistic yr3 ~$100-200k.
red_flags: Boutique GM and client terms are E
AI demand erosion acknowledged but unquantified
Conversion fees may need IL employment-agency license

rationale: Back-to-back buying keeps capital tiny and line-down urgency supports markups, but zero evidence on fee levels, request volume or find-rate. Radwell, distributor desks and buyers searching eBay/surplus themselves compete. Counterfeit liability. Plausible small desk at ~$60-120k; best as a wedge into plant accounts.

A-level Illinois rules cap fees at 10% and require a Treasurer license and fidelity bond, making outreach uneconomic; owners are skeptical and states promote free self-claims. One-off claims, slow payment. Record itself caps the milestone at $5k/mo.
red_flags: Profitability hinges on unverified other-state caps

rationale: No durable wedge, one-off deals, $3-8 per unit, sourcing capped by founder hours, and high account-suspension risk because retail receipts often fail authenticity checks. Record itself caps milestone at $5k/mo. Course-seller hype, not evidence.

Inspection mandate is A-level, but tariffs, contract values, buyer identity and vendor selection are all MISSING. Concentrated IEP/terminal buyers with entrenched vendors, procurement and safety walls, possible union environment, net 45-60 vs weekly crew payroll. Upper launch capital exceeds $100k. If won, contracts are sticky.

Capacity shortage helps access, but new-carrier insurance premiums are unquantified and rising, owner-operators scarce, accidents can cancel coverage, and dray rates are cyclical with import volumes. Capital/insurance-heavy with net-30 vs weekly O/O pay. Record shows $0 low case.

Strong B-level FDD data, but it shows single-territory owner income only 2-11% of revenue; royalty add-back mostly gets spent on self-run marketing. Demand is real and paid-on-completion, but skilled craftsmen are scarce and licensed-trade scope creep is a legal risk. Realistic independent yr3 ~$50-110k.

Small niche add-on: $200-300 courses, 5-year refresher cycle, moderate competition incl. university program, accreditation and instructor requirements MISSING. Prepaid and cheap to start, but record itself tops out at ~$50k and $5k/mo.

A-level LTV ($873/MA policy, falling) and CMS caps anchor economics; license obtainable in weeks. But national call centers and captive agents dominate, CMS rules limit outreach, commission cuts and DOJ scrutiny hit book value. 150-300 sales/yr for a new field agent is optimistic; realistic yr3 ~$70-150k, personality-driven.

Real shortage and sticky multi-year contracts, but zero spending evidence: outsourcing prevalence, contract values, margins all MISSING. Public RFPs demand references a newcomer lacks, 9 months to first revenue, net 30-60 public pay vs biweekly payroll float, IMRF/TRS and DTLSA questions unresolved.

Customer-funded drop-ship cash cycle is attractive, but ranking against Grainger, McMaster, Amazon and national catalogs is the whole problem; reseller approval and allowed margins unconfirmed. $66 per $300 order before ads. Realistic yr3 ~$20-60k.

Plausible niche with recurring annual reconciliations and AI lease abstraction leverage, but no fee, recovery or incumbent data at all. Anti-contingency-auditor lease clauses could block the model; recoveries often come as rent credits, delaying fees. Small per-lease dollars need large portfolios.

Crowded CPG category with weak defensibility; even BARK at 62% GM loses money. Wholesale to independents gives small orders, needs hundreds of doors, state feed registrations and recall exposure; imported chews tariff-exposed. Record shows negative low case and $10k/mo ceiling.

Attractive take rates and buyer-funded float, with A-level incumbent economics (RB Global 15.5% op margin) - but those are incumbent figures. Two-sided cold start versus Purple Wave, BigIron, GovDeals and local auctioneers; consignor trust takes years. Illinois auctioneer licensing requirements MISSING; titled vehicles may need dealer license.

Founder cannot be the FMC Qualifying Individual, so must hire one plus post $75k/$50k financial responsibility before volume. 8-20% margin, extreme competition from Flexport and thousands of NVOCCs, prepaid ocean freight vs SMB terms, trade-policy whiplash. De minimis tailwind real but demand capture unquantified.

Cheap, prepaid autopay, simple SOP labor and route density are genuine strengths, but no Item 19 or pricing data retrieved and Chicago winters cause pauses/churn. Small tickets cap a metro at ~$0.5-1M revenue; realistic yr3 owner profit ~$40-70k. A good side route, not a holding-company base.

One-time purchases, fragmented per-state content, copyrighted code books, entrenched brands (Mike Holt) and free AI tutoring eroding paid prep (Chegg -39%). Founder lacks trade-code expertise. Record shows $0 low case and $10k/mo ceiling.

A-level terms are unfavorable: 50% renewal royalty, franchisor owns policies, franchise count falling ~9-10%/yr, Illinois hail rate pressure, 30 months to profitability, and franchisor prefers experienced agents. Item 19 not reviewed. No terminal book value for a holding-company base.

Retainers are cash-positive and fees large, but buyers require a placement track record and executive network the founder lacks; record itself says only viable as evolution of a proven desk. Partner-limited, relationship-bound, PE-cycle exposed; fee conventions unsourced. Base case for a newcomer is near-zero mandates in year 1.
red_flags: Win rate for new boutiques unknown

rationale: Compliance-driven recurring demand with B-level incumbent data (Transcat 32.5% service GM) and a real roll-up exit market. But needs an experienced metrologist hire, capital in standards before revenue, and 17025 accreditation cost/time MISSING while many buyers require it. Slow 18-month breakeven; durable once established.
red_flags: Incumbent GM may overstate new-entrant margin

rationale: Engineering background genuinely fits documentation work and capital is small, but no fee or market data retrieved. Crowded with CPA practices and specialist/tech-enabled firms; CPAs may internalize rather than refer. Heightened IRS documentation scrutiny, refund-on-disallowance risk, 3-12 month fee lag, CPA partner needed for sign-off.

Walk-in, on-the-spot decisions by thousands of independent owners make access easy and route roles delegate well. But no rack-jobber economics retrieved, consignment inventory spread across stores with shrink, tariff-exposed imported goods, low-ticket impulse categories and declining independents. Realistic yr3 ~$50-90k; per-store sales assumed.

Real aftertreatment maintenance need and concentrated shop buyers, but pricing, equipment cost and local competitors all MISSING; dealers and HD parts distributors already bundle cleaning. Capex plus exchange-unit inventory before utilisation; cracked-filter liability. Plausible small regional service; upside unproven.

Supply is abundant (A) but the whole business depends on trusted overseas buyer networks the founder lacks; record admits this. Trust-heavy one-off deals, payment fraud, sanctions/export-control exposure, valuation errors. $0 low case, no demand evidence.

Monthly prepaid memberships help cash, but $50-120k lease/build-out at risk, 18-month ramp to ~100 students, national brands (Mathnasium, Kumon) and AI tutors compressing willingness to pay. No Item 19 or pricing retrieved. Discretionary family spend; realistic yr3 ~$30-80k per centre.

Prepaid and cheap, but chicken-and-egg candidate liquidity against Indeed/LinkedIn/Google, no pricing or fill-rate evidence, hiring-cycle exposure. Record shows $0 low case and $10k/mo ceiling. Best as a lead source for staffing/training lines.

Recurring carrier need, but concentrated, consolidated buyers with 3-12 month vendor qualification and track-record walls; $75-350 per assignment at 20-40% GM is thin; net 30-60. No vendor pricing retrieved. Virtual-audit AI wedge is plausible but replicable by incumbents.

Low-ticket ($2-6 per employee-year, unverified) service that payroll/HR incumbents bundle at little or no cost; easy automation also lowers barriers for rivals. No pricing data, IDES hearing representation rules unverified. Record caps at $10k/mo.

Plausible demo-driven specialty service with recurring mold/food-line programs, but pricing and utilization MISSING; equipment idles without dense recurring demand. PE-backed industrial cleaning platforms consolidating nearby. ~$1,000/day contribution is E; realistic yr3 ~$50-90k per crew. Confined-space CO2 safety risk.

Residual commission book can compound into real equity value with low capital, and commission sales roles delegate. But commission norms, ICC ABC license terms and saturation are all unverified; commercial buyers suffer heavy broker fatigue; clawbacks and Illinois deceptive-marketing enforcement history. Realistic yr3 ~$60-150k.
Extremely saturated Etsy category with no wedge, labor-bound production, single-platform dependence, fee levels unverified. Record caps at $5k/mo. Fine hobby income, not a holding-company base.

OSHA annual crane inspection mandate is A-level and recurring, capital is light, and inspector scarcity is a barrier once staffed. But pricing and local crane population MISSING, founder must hire scarce qualified inspectors, missed-defect liability and insurance cost unverified, construction-cycle exposure. Inspector-bound scaling.

Consignment with buyer-funded float and low capital; liquidation demand is mildly counter-cyclical and referral channels (brokers, lenders, trustees) are identifiable. Incumbent data is A but small-operator GMV and take rates are E. Illinois auctioneer licensing/online exemption unresolved; local online auctioneers already serve small closings.

Essential, recession-resilient, cash-at-use and commonly semi-absentee, but a $300k-1M new build with personally guaranteed equipment financing far exceeds the capital boundary before first revenue; record itself estimates 10-25% ROIC. No industry data retrieved. Site risk and utility inflation.
red_flags: Personal guarantee depends on founder credit

rationale: Healthcare entry-job demand is real, but low tuition ($1-2.5k), heavy community-college price competition, externship-site dependency, costly consumer marketing, IBHE approval unverified and 9 months to first revenue. Record caps at $10k/mo. For-profit school scrutiny adds risk.

Referral/rev-share economics entirely MISSING; 3-9 month mid-market cycles, vendor-controlled terms, and record itself frames it as a feature of a bookkeeping firm with $0-60k range. Not a standalone business.

A-level statutes show the business of serving process effectively requires PI licensure (age 21 + 3 years experience + exam), so founder needs a licensed PI principal; 12 months to first revenue. Low ticket ($20-60 contribution), commodity pricing, local routes, e-service erosion. Record caps at $10k/mo.

Good C-level Census data that cuts against the idea: ~10% residual margin, ~$1.3M machinery per typical shop, materials/payroll heavy. 1-2 used machines yield thin profit until utilization is pre-sold; Section 232 metal tariffs, cyclical demand, machinist hiring, upper capital $250k. Sensible only as later vertical integration.

High office vacancy and diversion goals create steady lease-exit work, and mid-size projects below national players minimums are a credible wedge via CRE brokers. But pricing, resale values (cubicles near-worthless) and contribution are MISSING; labor-heavy with warehouse/inventory glut risk; movers may bundle cheaply. Realistic yr3 ~$70-140k.

Sympathetic need with an aging tailwind, but size x style inventory breadth, MOQs, slow turns, sizing returns and high apparel tariffs make it capital-hungry; major brands already run adaptive lines. Even FIGS earns thin operating margins. Record shows negative low case and $10k/mo ceiling.

rationale: Consumable, safety-driven demand and reachable fleets, but $80-180k in service trucks and tire inventory for thin 18-35% margins, newcomer distributor pricing uncertain, and national commercial tire dealers dominate fleet programs. Tire margins MISSING; used-tire rules unverified.

Many reachable local buyers and delegable dispatch work, but thin per-run margins, net-30 vs weekly driver pay, gig-platform undercutting (Roadie, GoShare, Frayt), worker-classification risk in Illinois, insurance costs. No pricing evidence. Record caps at $10k/mo.

Essential, climate-driven demand with recurring memberships and a large replacement profit pool; regional roll-up multiples exist. But no FDD/10-K data retrieved, founder must hire a scarce lead tech, PE-backed rivals bid up paid search, municipal licensing MISSING. Realistic yr3 ~$100-200k if techs retained; strong if executed.

Survey-methods fit for founder and prepaid, but sample-building is the hard part, associations already publish many surveys, small niche market, pricing unverified. Record shows $0-60k and $5k/mo ceiling. A content asset, not a base business.

Contingency B2B collections is low-capital and mildly counter-cyclical, with vertical specialization (freight, contractors) as a wedge. But fee rates, recovery rates and Illinois Collection Agency Act scope/bond/manager rules are all unverified; multi-state licensing and trust accounting add compliance load.

Zero capital and good writing/research fit, but hours-based, crowded with freelancers, budget-constrained buyers, federal funding volatility, and LLM drafting commoditizes the core product. Post-award compliance is the better wedge but still labor-bound. Record caps at $10k/mo.

Customer-required FAI/PPAP gives a real but episodic overflow need; CMM capex (up to $150k) before utilization, a hired CMM programmer, and no rate or volume data. Local, low-moderate ceiling; best as an adjunct to calibration or brokerage.

Urgent-need buyers search actively and 24/7 small-job response is a plausible wedge, but rental rates, utilization and seasonality are all MISSING; fleet capital is at risk before demand proven, and national renters plus restoration contractors owning gear compete. Weather-driven volatility; idle fleet in mild seasons.

Loyal, need-driven buyers in reachable communities, but scarce dedicated co-packers with prepaid runs, 30-45% GM, trade spend, 24-month breakeven, and a single cross-contact incident could be existential. Small CPG brands like Laird lose money. Record shows negative low case and $10k/mo ceiling.

Pennies-per-gallon margins (3-10% GM) on $100-250k of fuel trucks plus fuel working capital, hazmat CDL drivers, fire-marshal and fuel-tax licensing MISSING, spill/fire liability, entrenched competitors. Ryder figure is incumbent revenue, not margin. Record concedes weak entry strategy.

Genuine truck-parking scarcity, prepaid monthly rent, minimal staffing and a zoning-limited supply moat once a site is secured. But zoning/special-use approval is the binding constraint, land lease plus paving, lighting, fencing and stormwater can exceed $100k before revenue, and site-by-site scaling is capital-hungry. Demand data MISSING.

Urgent, non-discretionary need with high tickets ($500-2,500), paid on completion, low capital, and moderate competition (Critter Control plus locals). But pricing and IDNR permit requirements unverified, roof-work/rabies risk, seasonal swings, skilled exclusion techs harder to hire. Plausible yr3 ~$80-150k.

Event-driven, irregular demand tied to municipal hiring cycles, one-time purchases, low founder fit, free department prep sessions, written-exam drills AI-exposed, applicant volumes and prices MISSING. Record shows $0-50k and $5k/mo ceiling.

Near-zero capital and a sensible way to learn the supply base, but commission rates MISSING, commissions arrive 60-90 days after shop collects, principals often terminate reps once accounts are established, and it is a solo, founder-hour-capped role. Useful as a stepping stone to WS03-001, not a base business.

Dealers are easy to reach and buy quickly, but this is low-margin labor arbitrage at $40-250 per move with insurance cost and accident claims as the swing factor, FMCSA authority for car hauling, auto-sales cyclicality. No sources. Record caps at $10k/mo.
